summary: Large max_tokens runs timeout mid-generation and show inconsistent billed token counts
summary_detail: Customer reports repeated request timeouts when setting very large max_tokens (>=25000) during long-context generation. The request sometimes returns a partial chunk, connection closes, and billed tokens reported to the customer do not match the length of the partial output. Issue started after a traffic spike + model rollout last week.
description:
Issue summary:
- Requests with max_tokens >= 25000 intermittently time out mid-generation in production for LexiHealth (dedicated pool in us-east).

Impact:
- Multiple jobs aborted mid-generation resulting in partial outputs and customer-reported mismatch between observed output tokens and billing records. Several high-priority product workflows (clinical summarization batches) are affected; they rely on uninterrupted long generations.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (lexi-dedicated-us-east), prod.
- Models: redwood-v2-32k (pinned for customer), fallback to openx-30k occasionally.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-v2-32k and max_tokens=30000, prompt including 45k input tokens (medical transcript).
2) Use streaming=true and keep-connection-open semantics.
3) Observe progression for ~20-40s then abrupt close with HTTP 504 or stream reset.
4) Customer checks billing dashboard and sees billed token count lower than expected for completed tokens before the reset.

Observed behavior:
- Generation terminates mid-run with either 504 or stream reset depending on client network.
- Support logs show runtime worker marked as overloaded, then OOM-eviction-like scheduling event for that GPU during the run window.
- Billing events show a charged token window that stops earlier than the last chunk the customer received in the stream.

Expected behavior:
- Long runs should either complete or fail deterministically with clear billing attribution and a clear error returned. Streaming clients should receive a terminal error chunk indicating failure and billing should reflect tokens successfully emitted or an explicit aborted-charge policy.

Logs / artifacts provided by customer:
- Customer provided full request/response stream (truncated) and billing invoice snapshot (attachments in ticket).
- Sample request id: req-lexi-20260307-9bx2
- Time window: 2026-03-06T21:10:00Z to 2026-03-06T21:13:00Z

Initial notes:
- The behavior is not strictly a pure "timeout on long tail" — the runtime appears to evict or preempt long-running KV/cache state under high memory pressure which causes an internal worker to restart mid-generation. Our edge gateways sometimes detect the restart as a stream error, which leads to disparate client-side behavior. Billing pipeline uses a separate token-commit path which appears to have not been flushed for the last streamed chunks in several reproductions.

Customer impact classification:
- High (workloads failing for a critical customer workflow).
comments: 2026-03-07 Priya Shah (Support): Customer reports intermittent mid-generation failures and billing mismatch. Provided request id and billing screenshot. Escalating to SRE and Serving Runtime team.

2026-03-08 Miguel Torres (SRE): Reproduced locally with a synthetic 40k token prompt against redwood-v2-32k on a test dedicated pool. Observed worker eviction around 36s correlated with GPU memory pressure and an internal cache truncation event. Captured runtime logs and heap traces. Filed initial hypothesis: preemptive cache eviction + incomplete billing flush.

2026-03-09 Elena Park (Runtime Eng): Confirmed eviction pattern. Noted recent kernel selection change in rollout PR #811 that alters KV cache retention policy for very long sequences. Suspect regression in the fallback kernel causing memory blow-up for certain sequence lengths. Added debug flags to trace kernel selection path.

2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Scoped impact to dedicated pools with workloads that pin sessions for >30s continuous generation. No evidence of this happening on hosted multi-tenant pools so far. Recommended temporary mitigation: lower max_tokens to <=12k or use chunked generation with stateful resume API. Also suggested increasing worker memory headroom for lexid-1 pool until fix deployed.

2026-03-12 Priya Shah: Customer accepted temporary mitigation (split jobs) but requested timeline for permanent fix and a billing reconciliation. Open to a credit for affected runs pending verification.

2026-03-12 Elena Park: Implemented a hotfix branch to revert the kernel selection tweak; running canary in lexid-1 with synthetic load. If stable for 24h will promote to prod and update billing flush path to flush token-commits at stream chunk boundaries to prevent undercounting on abrupt worker restarts.
2026-03-12 Miguel Torres: Added linked internal ticket INT-1102 to track capacity increase and billing pipeline change. Planning a postmortem if canary confirms fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis chain: 1) Recent rollout changed kernel selection for long sequences; 2) Under certain input length distributions the chosen kernel increases temporary KV/cache footprint beyond safe threshold; 3) Worker scheduler preempts/evicts the worker which closes the stream, and the billing commit path (async) may not have flushed the last emitted chunks before eviction; 4) Results in apparent discrepancy for customer and a mid-run timeout. Evidence: reproducer logs, heap traces, and correlation with PR 811.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: recommended customer split large generations into smaller chunks and/or reduce max_tokens. Applied temporary capacity increase to lexid-1 dedicated pool to reduce OOM evictions. Hotfix: reverted kernel-selection change in canary and added an explicit token-commit flush at stream chunk boundaries. If canary passes 24h with synthetic and customer traffic, schedule production rollout and issue billing reconciliation for affected runs (pending verification). Detailed postmortem to follow.
